title: Spinal Cord Injury (SCI)
qa: Patient with C6 complete injury: what grasp can be trained? Tenodesis grasp: active wrist extension passively closes the fingers.
Why not stretch finger flexors with the wrist extended in C6 injury? It would lengthen them and lose the tenodesis effect.
A T4 patient becomes flushed with a severe headache and BP 190/110. Action? Autonomic dysreflexia: sit up, loosen clothing, check bladder and catheter, call medical help.
What does AIS C mean? Motor incomplete with most key muscles below the level weaker than grade 3.
Why maintain hamstring length? To allow long sitting for dressing and transfers.

redFlags.Finding: Sudden pounding headache, high BP, flushing and sweating above the injury, slow heart rate (injury at T6 or above)
redFlags.Immediate action: Sit the patient up, lower legs, loosen tight clothing and straps, check bladder (catheter kinked or full bladder) and bowel, monitor BP, call medical help
Recline, raise legs; use binder and stockings; progress slowly

redFlags.Finding: Redness that does not fade after pressure is removed
New loss of function above the level

modalityNotes: FES cycling and FES-assisted walking in selected patients; standing frames for weight-bearing and wellbeing.
